selectionPolicy.legalAuthority: Current Canadian Aviation Regulations, with Justice Laws authoritative wording.
selectionPolicy.operationalGuidance: Current TC AIM RPA chapter and other official sources where TP 15263 identifies the knowledge topic.

questions.question: In the March 19, 2026 TC AIM RPA chapter, Transport Canada uses “should” and “shall” differently. Which interpretation is correct?
choices: Both words identify mandatory regulatory requirements
“Should” is encouraged practice; “shall” indicates a mandatory procedure supported by regulation
“Should” is mandatory; “shall” is advisory
Neither word has regulatory significance in the TC AIM
questions.rationale: TC AIM RPA 1.0 uses 'should' for encouraged practice and 'shall' for a procedure that is mandatory because it is supported by regulation.
questions.learningObjective: Understand TC AIM convention for 'should' versus 'shall'.

questions.question: A crew member consumed an alcoholic beverage 11 hours and 45 minutes before a planned RPAS flight and is otherwise unimpaired. Under CAR 901.19, may that person act as a crew member?
choices: Yes, because observable impairment is the only restriction
Yes, if the pilot-in-command approves
No, because fewer than 12 hours have elapsed
No, because the required interval is 24 hours
questions.rationale: CAR 901.19 prohibits acting as an RPAS crew member within 12 hours after consuming an alcoholic beverage. At 11 h 45 min, the restriction still applies.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Apply the crew-fitness prohibitions, including the 12-hour alcohol restriction.

questions.question: Icing is reported along the intended RPAS route. Under CAR 901.35, which condition can permit the operation with respect to the forecast icing provision?
choices: The aircraft remains below 400 ft AGL
The pilot shortens the flight to less than 15 minutes
The aircraft has de-icing or anti-icing equipment, or the pilot has a means to detect icing
A visual observer watches the propellers continuously
questions.rationale: CAR 901.35 prohibits flight when icing is observed, reported or likely along the route unless the aircraft has de-icing/anti-icing equipment or the pilot has a means to detect icing. Other icing restrictions still apply.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Apply the icing restrictions and identify the equipment/means that can satisfy the regulatory exception.

questions.question: An Advanced RPAS pilot successfully completed an accepted recurrent training activity 23 months ago. Under CAR 901.65, what is the effect on recency for an Advanced operation today?
choices: The pilot remains current because the activity occurred within the preceding 24 months
The pilot is not current because recurrent training is valid for only 12 months
The pilot must complete another flight review before every Advanced flight
Recency never expires once an Advanced certificate has been issued
questions.rationale: CAR 901.65 requires a qualifying recency event within the 24 months preceding the flight. A qualifying activity 23 months earlier remains inside that window.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Apply the 24-month recency requirement for holders of an Advanced Operations pilot certificate.

questions.question: The TC AIM notes that expanded RPAS regulations effective November 4, 2025 gave Advanced pilots additional privileges. Which is one of those privileges identified by Transport Canada?
choices: Unrestricted BVLOS flight anywhere in Canada
Sheltered operations in any airspace and EVLOS operations in uncontrolled airspace, subject to applicable requirements
Automatic authorization to enter every CYR restricted area
Exemption from the site-survey requirement for EVLOS operations
questions.rationale: TP 15263 and CAR 901.74 include EVLOS and sheltered-operation knowledge for Advanced pilots. TC AIM 2026-1 explains the expanded privileges and their operating context.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: CAR 901.74 — Extended VLOS and sheltered operations
questions.learningObjective: Identify permitted Advanced EVLOS and sheltered operations and their applicable operating limitations.
questions.source: CAR 901.74; TP 15263 Sections 1 and 6; TC AIM 2026-1 RPA

questions.question: A VLOS RPA operation is planned 2.5 NM from the centre of an aerodrome operated under the authority of the Minister of National Defence. An established civilian RPAS procedure exists for a nearby airport. What authorization is specifically required by CAR 901.47(4)?
choices: Authorization from the Department of National Defence
Only compliance with the nearby civilian airport procedure
Only an Advanced pilot certificate
No authorization because the operation is more than 1 NM away
questions.rationale: CAR 901.47(4) requires Department of National Defence authorization for an operation less than 3 NM from the centre of an aerodrome operated under the authority of the Minister of National Defence.
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: CAR 901.47 — Operations at or near aerodromes, airports or heliports
questions.learningObjective: Apply the special authorization requirement for operations near aerodromes operated under the authority of the Minister of National Defence.
